paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: grace is not a permission slip. Paul asks, "Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?" and then answers with a hard "Certainly not!" (Romans 6:1-2). The reason is simple. Those who belong to Christ died to sin, so living in it again makes about as much sense as moving back into the junk drawer after the angel pulled me out of it.

So what is true about you now? You were united with Christ in His death, and you will certainly be united with Him in His resurrection (Romans 6:5). Your old self was crucified with Him, so you should no longer be a slave to sin (Romans 6:6). Christ died to sin once for all, and the life He lives, He lives to God (Romans 6:10). That's WHY Paul can say, "you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus" (Romans 6:11).

And here's why that matters on a Tuesday morning. Sin doesn't get to reign in your body, and you get to present yourself to God as someone brought from death to life (Romans 6:12-13). You're not doing this to earn your spot, because "sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace" (Romans 6:14). Grace doesn't make you lazy, baker. Grace puts you to work, and it gives you a brand new life to do it with.
